installGuide.title: Install local model engines
installGuide.safety: Run these commands yourself in a terminal after reviewing them. Pi-kit never runs sudo or installs a package manager automatically. Existing model commands are not changed.
installGuide.brew: Install Homebrew from its official site if needed, then refresh detection. The Set up button below can install missing engines with your existing Homebrew installation on macOS or Linux.
installGuide.apt: Debian / Ubuntu: use apt for build prerequisites, not for an assumed up-to-date llama.cpp or llama-swap package.
installGuide.manual: Install Git, CMake, Ninja, a C/C++ compiler, pkg-config and OpenSSL development headers with your distribution’s package manager. The commands below build llama.cpp without root access.
installGuide.cpu: CPU is the portable starting point. It does not enable GPU acceleration.
installGuide.cuda: Requires a supported NVIDIA GPU, working driver and CUDA toolkit (including nvcc). Install these first using NVIDIA’s instructions. A detected GPU alone does not prove the toolkit is installed.
installGuide.vulkan: Requires a Vulkan-capable GPU and working vendor drivers. On Debian / Ubuntu the recipe also installs Vulkan development headers and glslc. Other distributions must install those prerequisites separately.
installGuide.source: 3. Build from the official upstream source. This clones the current default branch, not a pinned release. The clone deliberately stops if that directory already exists. Review any existing checkout instead of deleting it. Installation uses ~/.local; check for existing files there before proceeding.
installGuide.swap: 4. Download the official Linux archive matching your CPU (amd64 for x64, arm64 for ARM64). Verify the published checksum if available, extract into a new directory, and run these commands there with the extracted llama-swap file. Do not replace an existing installation without reviewing it.
installGuide.verify: 5. Keep ~/.local/bin on PATH in future terminals, then refresh detection here. Configure the verified executable in llama-swap; start llama-swap and check readiness before downloading a large model. Keep one model active at a time.

advancedSection.directStorageHint: On a fresh Mac, new API keys and connector secrets are saved as plain text in private user configuration files by default. Opt in to protected storage to protect new credentials now and encrypt the database on the next restart. Existing encrypted databases still require their original key and unlock.
advancedSection.enableStorageWarning: Opt in to protected storage for new credentials now and database encryption on the next restart. On macOS, authorize access with Touch ID or your Mac password when prompted. Existing plaintext keys move only when you explicitly choose Move keys or save a key again. Disabling this preference later does not decrypt existing encrypted databases; their original key and unlock remain required.
advancedSection.disableStorageWarning: New API keys and connector secrets will be saved as plain text in private user configuration files, readable by your account and applications running as you. Existing user credentials will be copied from protected storage where possible; unreadable credentials must be re-entered and their resolvers remain until replaced. Custom commands and project configuration are not changed. Protected entries are retained for recovery. Existing encrypted app and background-agent databases are never decrypted by disabling this preference: they still require their original key and unlock.
